issues.description: The problem specification (UML and textual description) declares Milkable.messageOnMilk() as returning a boolean (indicating whether milking succeeded), but the solution implements Milkable.messageOnMilk() returning a String and the concrete classes (Seal, Goat) return Strings. This mismatch will confuse students: they may implement a boolean-returning method per the specification and then face compilation/test failures or mismatch with the provided solution/tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across all artifacts. Either change the problem statement/UML to specify messageOnMilk() returns String (and adjust textual description to match), or change the solution and concrete implementations to have messageOnMilk() return boolean and adapt tests and song/text output accordingly. Prefer updating the problem statement to expect a String if the intent is to print a milking message.

issues.description: The template Farm.java declares singFarmSongVerse without an Animal parameter (the parameter is commented out), whereas the UML/problem statement and the solution implement singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). This inconsistency in the template method signature can confuse students about the expected method parameter and interferes with implementing the verse printing logic that requires the Animal instance.
issues.suggestedFix: Uncomment or add the Animal parameter in the template's singFarmSongVerse signature so it matches the UML and the solution (private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)). Ensure template body uses the parameter consistently. This removes confusion and aligns the template with the intended design.

issues.description: The problem statement (both the UML and the textual task description) specifies that Milkable.messageOnMilk() returns a boolean (true/false), while the template usage and the solution define and use messageOnMilk() as returning a String message. This mismatch means students following the problem text would implement a boolean-returning method, but the provided template Main and the reference solution expect and print a String. This creates a direct mapping/confusion between the requirement and the code-level API.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the API across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement and UML to specify messageOnMilk(): String and describe the expected message content (e.g., "Goat [name] is milked"), or (B) change the template and solution to make Milkable.messageOnMilk() return boolean and update usages (e.g., Main and sing logic) accordingly. Preferred: update the problem statement/UML to expect String to match template and solution.
